thought_title: He Truly Suffered; They Only Seem

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα ἔπαθεν δἰ ἡμᾶς, ἵνα σωθῶμεν: καὶ ἀληθῶς ἔπαθεν, ὡς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν, οὐχ ὥσπερ ἄπιστοί τινες λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, αὐτοὶ το δοκεῖν ὄντες: καὶ καθὼς φρονοῦσιν, καὶ συμβήσεται αὐτοῖς, οὖσιν ἀσωμάτοις καὶ δαιμονικοῖς.
pass_a_gloss: [1] For he suffered all these things for our sake, so that we might be saved. And he truly suffered, just as he also truly raised himself, not as some unbelievers say, that he suffered in appearance, while they themselves exist in appearance. And just as they think, so it will also happen to them: they will be without bodies and like demons.

lemmas.gloss: raise up (transitive, here reflexive with ἑαυτόν)

pass_b_english: All of this he suffered for us, so that we might be saved. And he suffered truly, just as he truly raised himself. Some unbelievers say his suffering was only an appearance. No, it is they who are only an appearance! And what they believe will become their lot: they will end up bodiless, like the demons.

choices.term: τὸ δοκεῖν … αὐτοὶ τὸ δοκεῖν ὄντες
choices.english: only an appearance … it is they who are only an appearance
choices.why: Ignatius turns the docetists' slogan back on them; kept as two short blows.
rejected: only seem to be Christians (ANF supplies 'Christians')

choices.why: Active, reflexive: Christ as agent of his own rising; not smoothed into passive.
Two predicates kept; 'like the demons' renders the adjective without inventing 'evil spirits' as a noun class.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF supplies '[Christians]' after 'only seem to be'; the Greek has no noun, so this draft leaves the barb bare.

notes: Span: whole of Smyrnaeans 2 (sections 1); old ANF span covers the full chapter.
Pack topic: passion-resurrection. Same chapter English is shared by every excerpt id on this chapter.
Pack Greek prints 'δἰ' (for δι’) and 'το δοκεῖν' without accent; copied as printed.

checker_dispute: checker b says Pass A misreads 'οὐχ ὥσπερ ἄπιστοί τινες λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, αὐτοὶ το δοκεῖν ὄντες'. Pass A gives the unbelievers' claim as 'that he suffered in appearance' (τὸ δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, accusative-infinitive after λέγουσιν) and the retort 'while they themselves exist in appearance' (αὐτοὶ … ὄντες, nominative participle agreeing with ἄπιστοί τινες). That is the Greek structure; Pass B states the same turn-back as 'it is they who are only an appearance'. Checker b itself grants Pass B is right and the two passes say the same thing. Text kept, consistent with the other Smyrnaeans 2 ids.

review.notes: Checked locked Smyrnaeans 2 paragraph 1 against both passes. 'Ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα ἔπαθεν δἰ ἡμᾶς, ἵνα σωθῶμεν' is A 'For he suffered all these things for our sake, so that we might be saved' and B 'All of this he suffered for us, so that we might be saved'. 'ἀληθῶς ἔπαθεν, ὡς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν' keeps Christ as agent in both ('raised himself'), not a passive rising. 'οὐχ ὥσπερ ἄπιστοί τινες λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, αὐτοὶ το δοκεῖν ὄντες' is A 'not as some unbelievers say, that he suffered in appearance, while they themselves exist in appearance' and B 'Some unbelievers say his suffering was only an appearance. No, it is they who are only an appearance' — same negation and turn-back. 'καὶ καθὼς φρονοῦσιν, καὶ συμβήσεται αὐτοῖς, οὖσιν ἀσωμάτοις καὶ δαιμονικοῖς' is A 'just as they think, so it will also happen to them: they will be without bodies and like demons' and B 'what they believe will become their lot: they will end up bodiless, like the demons'. Notes disclose printed 'δἰ' and unaccented 'το δοκεῖν'. No scripture is quoted, so no citation is missing or false. Title names the anti-docetic thought.

Source identity: Locked Greek matches Ignatius, Smyrnaeans 2. Completeness: All clauses from the single paragraph are rendered in both Pass A and Pass B. Negation: 'οὐχ' correctly rendered as 'not' in Pass A and implied in Pass B's 'No'. Agency: Christ as agent of his own raising ('ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν') preserved in both passes. Modality: Indicative mood preserved; no modal verbs added. Doctrine: Docetist error and orthodox response accurately conveyed. Scripture: No scriptural citations present, so check passes by default. Title: 'He Truly Suffered; They Only Seem' names the thought, not just locus. Notes disclose OCR issues: 'δἰ' for δι’, 'το δοκεῖν' without accent. Pass A and B are consistent; checker dispute resolved in notes. Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties or reasons for failure.
